title: नवनवतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 99 · Ninth day: Bhishma at midday

summary.en: At midday the slaughter around Bhishma and the Somakas becomes terrible, and Bhishma cuts down hundreds of Pandava soldiers. Sanjaya says the carnage comes from fate and the king's own policy.
summary.kn: ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಭೀಷ್ಮ ಮತ್ತು ಸೋಮಕರ ನಡುವಿನ ಹತ್ಯೆ ಭಯಂಕರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಭೀಷ್ಮ ನೂರಾರು ಪಾಂಡವ ಸೈನಿಕರನ್ನು ಕಡಿಯುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಈ ಸಂಹಾರ ದೈವ ಮತ್ತು ರಾಜನ ತಪ್ಪು ನೀತಿಯಿಂದ ಬಂದದ್ದು ಎಂದು ಸಂಜಯ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: मध्याह्न में भीष्म और सोमकों के बीच संहार भयंकर हो जाता है और भीष्म सैकड़ों पाण्डव सैनिकों को काटते हैं। संजय कहते हैं कि यह विनाश दैव और राजा की अपनी नीति का फल है।
summary.te: మధ్యాహ్నం భీష్ముడు, సోమకుల మధ్య సంహారం భయంకరమవుతుంది; భీష్ముడు వందలాది పాండవ సైనికులను నరుకుతాడు. ఈ విధ్వంసం దైవం, రాజు అనీతి వల్లనని సంజయుడు చెబుతాడు.
summary.ta: நண்பகலில் பீஷ்மருக்கும் சோமகருக்கும் இடையிலான படுகொலை கொடுமையாகிறது; பீஷ்மர் நூற்றுக்கணக்கான பாண்டவ வீரரை வெட்டுகிறார். இவ்வழிவு விதியாலும் மன்னனின் தவறான கொள்கையாலும் வந்தது என்று சஞ்சயன் கூறுகிறான்.
summary.ml: ഉച്ചയ്ക്ക് ഭീഷ്മരെയും സോമകരെയും ചുറ്റിയുള്ള കൂട്ടക്കൊല ഭയങ്കരമാകുന്നു; ഭീഷ്മർ നൂറുകണക്കിന് പാണ്ഡവ സൈനികരെ വെട്ടിവീഴ്ത്തുന്നു. ഈ നാശം വിധിയിൽനിന്നും രാജാവിന്റെ സ്വന്തം നയത്തിൽനിന്നുമാണ് വരുന്നതെന്ന് സഞ്ജയൻ പറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.99; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
मध्याह्ने तु महाराज संग्रामः समपद्यत ।
लोकक्षयकरो रौद्रो भीष्मस्य सह सोमकैः ॥

meaning.en: At midday, great king, a dreadful battle began between Bhishma and the Somakas, one that brought ruin to the world.

verses.text:
गाङ्गेयो रथिनां श्रेष्ठः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् ।
व्यधमन्निशितैर्बाणैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥

meaning.en: The son of Ganga, best of charioteers, shattered the Pandava army with sharp arrows, by hundreds and thousands.

verses.text:
संममर्द च तत्सैन्यं पिता देवव्रतस्तव ।
धान्यानामिव लूनानां प्रकरं गोगणा इव ॥

meaning.en: Your father Devavrata crushed that army as herds of cattle trample heaps of harvested grain.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च विराटो द्रुपदस्तथा ।
भीष्ममासाद्य समरे शरैर्जघ्नुर्महारथम् ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin, Virata, and Drupada came up against Bhishma in the battle and struck that great chariot-warrior with arrows.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नं ततो विद्ध्वा विराटं च त्रिभिः शरैः ।
द्रुपदस्य च नाराचं प्रेषयामास भारत ॥

meaning.en: Piercing Dhrishtadyumna and Virata with three arrows each, Bhishma, Bharata, sent an iron arrow at Drupada.

verses.text:
तेन विद्धा महेष्वासा भीष्मेणामित्रकर्शिना ।
चुक्रुधुः समरे राजन्पादस्पृष्टा इवोरगाः ॥

meaning.en: Struck by Bhishma, tormentor of foes, those great archers grew furious in the battle, O king, like snakes trodden on.

verses.text:
शिखण्डी तं च विव्याध भरतानां पितामहम् ।
स्त्रीमयं मनसा ध्यात्वा नास्मै प्राहरदच्युतः ॥

meaning.en: Shikhandin also pierced the grandsire of the Bharatas; but Bhishma, thinking of him in his mind as a woman, did not strike him back.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु समरे क्रोधादग्निरिव ज्वलन् ।
पितामहं त्रिभिर्बाणैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत् ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtadyumna, blazing with anger in the battle like fire, struck the grandsire with three arrows in the arms and chest.

verses.text:
द्रुपदः पञ्चविंशत्या विराटो दशभिः शरैः ।
शिखण्डी पञ्चविंशत्या भीष्मं विव्याध सायकैः ॥

meaning.en: Drupada pierced Bhishma with twenty-five arrows, Virata with ten, and Shikhandin with twenty-five.

verses.text:
सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज भीष्मः संख्ये महात्मभिः ।
वसन्ते पुष्पशबलो रक्ताशोक इवाबभौ ॥

meaning.en: Sorely wounded in the battle by those great-souled ones, great king, Bhishma shone like a red ashoka tree dotted with blossoms in spring.

verses.text:
तान्प्रत्यविध्यद्गाङ्गेयस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः ।
द्रुपदस्य च भल्लेन धनुश्चिच्छेद मारिष ॥

meaning.en: The son of Ganga pierced each of them with three straight-flying arrows, and with a broad-headed arrow cut Drupada's bow, my lord.

verses.text:
सोऽन्यत्कार्मुकमादाय भीष्मं विव्याध पञ्चभिः ।
सारथिं च त्रिभिर्बाणैः सुशितै रणमूर्धनि ॥

meaning.en: Taking another bow, Drupada pierced Bhishma with five arrows and his charioteer with three very sharp ones at the head of the battle.

verses.text:
ततो भीमो महाराज द्रौपद्याः पञ्च चात्मजाः ।
केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च सात्यकिश्चैव सात्वतः ॥

meaning.en: Then Bhima, the five sons of Draupadi, the five Kekaya brothers, and Satyaki of the Satvatas,

verses.text:
अभ्यद्रवन्त गाङ्गेयं युधिष्ठिरहितेप्सया ।
रिरक्षिषन्तः पाञ्चाल्यं धृष्टद्युम्नमुखान्रणे ॥

meaning.en: rushed upon the son of Ganga, wishing to benefit Yudhishthira and to protect the Panchala Dhrishtadyumna and the others, who were being pressed in the battle.

verses.text:
तथैव तावकाः सर्वे भीष्मरक्षार्थमुद्यताः ।
प्रत्युद्ययुः पाण्डुसेनां सहसैन्या नराधिप ॥

meaning.en: In the same way all your men, eager to protect Bhishma, went with their troops against the Pandava army, O king.

verses.text:
तत्रासीत्सुमहद्युद्धं तव तेषां च संकुलम् ।
नराश्वरथनागानां यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम् ॥

meaning.en: There a very great and tangled fight took place between your men and theirs, swelling the realm of Yama with men, horses, chariots, and elephants.

verses.text:
रथी रथिनमासाद्य प्राहिणोद्यमसादनम् ।
तथेतरान्समासाद्य नरनागाश्वसादिनः ॥

meaning.en: Chariot-warriors met chariot-warriors and sent them to Yama's abode, and so did men, elephant-riders, and horsemen against their like.

verses.text:
अनयन्परलोकाय शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ।
अस्त्रैश्च विविधैर्घोरैस्तत्र तत्र विशां पते ॥

meaning.en: They sent each other to the other world with bent-jointed arrows and with terrible weapons of many kinds, here and there, lord of the people.

verses.text:
रथाश्च रथिभिर्हीना हतसारथयस्तथा ।
विप्रद्रुताश्वाः समरे दिशो जग्मुः समन्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Chariots, bereft of warriors, with their charioteers slain and horses bolting, ran in every direction in the battle.

verses.text:
मर्दमाना नरान्राजन्हयांश्च सुबहून्रणे ।
वातायमाना दृश्यन्ते गन्धर्वनगरोपमाः ॥

meaning.en: Crushing many men and horses in the fight, they were seen rushing like the wind, like cities in the air.

verses.text:
रथिनश्च रथैर्हीना वर्मिणस्तेजसा युताः ।
कुण्डलोष्णीषिणः सर्वे निष्काङ्गदविभूषिताः ॥

meaning.en: Chariot-warriors who had lost their chariots, armoured, radiant, all with earrings and turbans, adorned with necklaces and armlets,

verses.text:
देवपुत्रसमा रूपे शौर्ये शक्रसमा युधि ।
ऋद्ध्या वैश्रवणं चाति नयेन च बृहस्पतिम् ॥

meaning.en: like sons of the gods in beauty, like Shakra in battle, surpassing Kubera in wealth and Brihaspati in policy,

verses.text:
सर्वलोकेश्वराः शूरास्तत्र तत्र विशां पते ।
विप्रद्रुता व्यदृश्यन्त प्राकृता इव मानवाः ॥

meaning.en: lords of all the world, those heroes, here and there, lord of the people, were seen fleeing like common men.

verses.text:
दन्तिनश्च नरश्रेष्ठ विहीना वरसादिभिः ।
मृद्नन्तः स्वान्यनीकानि संपेतुः सर्वशब्दगाः ॥

meaning.en: Elephants too, best of men, bereft of their fine riders, trampling their own ranks, fell down, their cries of every kind.

verses.text:
वर्मभिश्चामरैश्छत्रैः पताकाभिश्च मारिष ।
कक्ष्याभिरथ तोत्त्रैश्च घण्टाभिस्तोमरैस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: With their armour, chowries, parasols, flags, girths, goads, bells, and tomaras scattered about,

verses.text:
विशीर्णैर्विप्रधावन्तो दृश्यन्ते स्म दिशो दश ।
नगमेघप्रतीकाशैर्जलदोदयनिस्वनैः ॥

meaning.en: they were seen running in all ten directions, looking like mountains or clouds, and rumbling like rising storm-clouds.

verses.text:
तथैव दन्तिभिर्हीनान्गजारोहान्विशां पते ।
प्रधावन्तोऽन्वपश्याम तव तेषां च संकुले ॥

meaning.en: In the same way, lord of the people, we saw elephant-riders whose elephants were gone running about in that tangle of your men and theirs.

verses.text:
नानादेशसमुत्थांश्च तुरगान्हेमभूषितान् ।
वातायमानानद्राक्षं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥

meaning.en: I saw horses from many lands, adorned with gold, by hundreds and thousands, running like the wind.

verses.text:
अश्वारोहान्हतैरश्वैर्गृहीतासीन्समन्ततः ।
द्रवमाणानपश्याम द्राव्यमाणांश्च संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: We saw horsemen whose horses were slain, swords in hand, fleeing on every side, and others being chased in the fight.

verses.text:
गजो गजं समासाद्य द्रवमाणं महारणे ।
ययौ विमृद्नंस्तरसा पदातीन्वाजिनस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: One elephant, meeting another in flight in that great battle, went on crushing foot-soldiers and horses in its force.

verses.text:
तथैव च रथान्राजन्संममर्द रणे गजः ।
रथश्चैव समासाद्य पदातिं तुरगं तथा ॥

meaning.en: And an elephant, O king, crushed chariots in the battle, and a chariot, meeting a foot-soldier or a horse,

verses.text:
व्यमृद्नात्समरे राजंस्तुरगांश्च नरान्रणे ।
एवं ते बहुधा राजन्प्रमृद्नन्तः परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: crushed horses and men in the fight, O king. So they ground one another down in many ways.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्रौद्रे तथा युद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये ।
प्रावर्तत नदी घोरा शोणितान्त्रतरङ्गिणी ॥

meaning.en: As that terrible and very fearsome battle went on, a dreadful river came into being, with waves of blood and entrails.

verses.text:
अस्थिसंचयसंघाटा केशशैवलशाद्वला ।
रथह्रदा शरावर्ता हयमीना दुरासदा ॥

meaning.en: Heaps of bones formed its shoals, hair was its moss and grass, chariots its pools, arrows its whirlpools, and horses its fish; it was hard to cross.

verses.text:
शीर्षोपलसमाकीर्णा हस्तिग्राहसमाकुला ।
कवचोष्णीषफेनाढ्या धनुर्द्वीपासिकच्छपा ॥

meaning.en: It was strewn with heads as rocks and thick with elephants as crocodiles, foaming with armour and turbans, with bows as its islands and swords as its turtles.

verses.text:
पताकाध्वजवृक्षाढ्या मर्त्यकूलापहारिणी ।
क्रव्यादसंघसंकीर्णा यमराष्ट्रविवर्धिनी ॥

meaning.en: Rich with flags and standards as trees, it swept away the banks of mortal men; crowded with flocks of flesh-eaters, it swelled the realm of Yama.

verses.text:
तां नदीं क्षत्रियाः शूरा हयनागरथप्लवैः ।
प्रतेरुर्बहवो राजन्भयं त्यक्त्वा महाहवे ॥

meaning.en: Brave Kshatriyas in numbers crossed that river on rafts of horses, elephants, and chariots, putting fear aside in the great battle.

verses.text:
अपोवाह रणे भीरून्कश्मलेनाभिसंवृतान् ।
यथा वैतरणी प्रेतान्प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: It carried away the cowardly in the battle, wrapped in faintness, as the Vaitarani carries the dead to the city of the king of the dead.

verses.text:
प्राक्रोशन्क्षत्रियास्तत्र दृष्ट्वा तद्वैशसं महत् ।
दुर्योधनापराधेन क्षयं गच्छन्ति कौरवाः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that great slaughter, the Kshatriyas there cried out, "The Kauravas are going to ruin through Duryodhana's fault!

verses.text:
गुणवत्सु कथं द्वेषं धार्तराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः ।
कृतवान्पाण्डुपुत्रेषु पापात्मा लोभमोहितः ॥

meaning.en: Why did Dhritarashtra's son, the lord of men, wicked-souled and deluded by greed, hate the virtuous sons of Pandu?"

verses.text:
एवं बहुविधा वाचः श्रूयन्ते स्मात्र भारत ।
पाण्डवस्तवसंयुक्ताः पुत्राणां ते सुदारुणाः ॥

meaning.en: Many such words, Bharata, were heard there, in praise of the Pandavas and very harsh to your sons.

verses.text:
ता निशम्य तदा वाचः सर्वयोधैरुदाहृताः ।
आगस्कृत्सर्वलोकस्य पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव ॥

meaning.en: Hearing those words spoken by all the warriors, your son Duryodhana, the offender against all the world,

verses.text:
भीष्मं द्रोणं कृपं चैव शल्यं चोवाच भारत ।
युध्यध्वमनहंकाराः किं चिरं कुरुथेति च ॥

meaning.en: said to Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, and Shalya, Bharata: "Fight without conceit! Why do you delay so long?"

verses.text:
ततः प्रववृते युद्धं कुरूणां पाण्डवैः सह ।
अक्षद्यूतकृतं राजन्सुघोरं वैशसं तदा ॥

meaning.en: Then the battle between the Kurus and the Pandavas, begun through the game of dice, raged on, terrible and murderous, O king.

verses.text:
यत्पुरा न निगृह्णीषे वार्यमाणो महात्मभिः ।
वैचित्रवीर्य तस्येदं फलं पश्य तथाविधम् ॥

meaning.en: Because you did not restrain him earlier, even when great-souled men were holding you back, son of Vichitravirya, see now the fruit of it.

verses.text:
न हि पाण्डुसुता राजन्ससैन्याः सपदानुगाः ।
रक्षन्ति समरे प्राणान्कौरवा वा विशां पते ॥

meaning.en: For neither the sons of Pandu with their troops and followers, nor the Kauravas, O lord of the people, are sparing their lives in the battle.

verses.text:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्घोरो वर्तते स्म जनक्षयः ।
दैवाद्वा पुरुषव्याघ्र तव चापनयान्नृप ॥

meaning.en: For this reason a dreadful slaughter of men is going on, either by fate or through your own mistaken policy, tiger among men.
